anchors.claim: typestr contains type plus name pointer and is also the hash mixing table.
hash_bucket reads raw typestr bytes, including relocated pointer bytes.
Hash-chain placement preserves reverse/immortal flag classes.
Forward lookup rotates only records with matching reverse/immortal flag class.
PTR lookup enumerates reverse records in bucket/chain order without moving the hash links.
Bulk reverse ownership and name-lookup temporary next links define the two-owner fixture.
Configured host-records use the same bulk add_hosts_entry path.
Wire PTR records are emitted in cache_find_by_addr order.
Non-debug TCP handling forks the current parent address space before tcp_request.

invariants: Exactly two .1 owners, x.test and y.test, with unchanged full record fields.
y.test has one reverse and one non-reverse record; A lookup cannot rotate across those flag classes.
No x.test/a.test forward queries, DHCP, HUP, inotify or generation mutation in this case.
PTR lookup changes temporary next links, not hash-chain order.
TCP inherits the unchanged parent initial namehash placement; one order applies across UDP and TCP.
